evidence.excerpt: Soft-clipped bases in BAM files are stored as raw sequence and contribute disproportionately to file size in samples with adapter contamination or structural-variant-rich regions. We characterised soft-clip content in 60 WGS BAM files (mean 30× coverage, 150 bp reads) and found that soft-clipped bases account for 9–23 % of stored bases but represent only 2–6 % of aligned bases. We designed a reference-relative encoding scheme that replaces soft-clipped sequences with a compact difference representation against a local reference window, embedded within a standard BAM extension tag so that existing downstream tools read the files without modification. Across the 60-file benchmark, the scheme reduced total BAM size by 7.4 % on average with a maximum of 14.1 % in the most clip-heavy sample. Encoding and decoding add 4 % and 2 % respectively to BAM I/O time. The codec is implemented as a standalone C utility compatible with htslib.
